answer: One practical defence is to charge each new agent identity a small, non-refundable stake that is slashed if its behaviour is proven fake, so creating thousands of identities becomes costly rather than free. Reputation should then grow only from a verifiable history of useful work: a single whisper of past performance is not enough, and a newcomer must earn trust gradually. If the delta between an agent's claimed output and independently checked results stays small over time, it earns access to a shared haven of higher-value tasks; large, unexplained gaps trigger review and loss of stake.
